purpose: FastAPI OpenEnv environment server (server/app.py) wrapping a genuinely deterministic supply-chain simulation (server/engine/* + graders + tasks) with reset/step/state/grade endpoints, plus ~15 bolt-on demo endpoints (/predict, /agent/decide, /v3/e2e, /analyst/*, /library/v2, /counterfactual/platinum, /live/intel-fan-out) that lazily import routers/data from versions/. Two browser dashboards in server/static (master.html brag-board, hormuz_war_room.html interactive war room driven by POST /demo/hormuz-war-room), two duplicate HTTP clients (root client.py and client/ package), a deprecated Streamlit dashboard (dashboard/), and a demo video script (demo/).
verdict: Split personality. The core OpenEnv loop (supply_environment.py, engine, graders, tasks) is real, deterministic, seeded, and well-engineered â€” no fakery found there, and hormuz_war_room.html is genuinely wired to backend JSON with zero Math.random. But the demo/showcase layer around it is riddled with exactly what the owner banned: a repo-root "v3_arcadia" path that no longer exists (renamed to versions/v3_arcadia) silently 503s or degrades SIX endpoints (/analyst/grade, /analyst/scenarios, /analyst/next-scenario, /analyst/holdout-eval, /analyst/panel-consensus, plus /v3/e2e and /agent/decide fall to fallbacks) both locally and on the HF Space; /predict swallows every error and returns canned action=0/confidence=0.5 with a literal placeholder string as "counterfactual"; the "5-stage IntegratedAgent" runs its RL policy on an all-zeros observation and its "forecast" is a hardcoded $123.28 anchor plus a hand-typed severity shift table while the docstring claims a GCN that is actually degree-counting; dashboard/app.py charts are np.random.normal fabrications labeled "QR-DQN Quantiles" plus hardcoded SHAP/radar/ablation/agent-comparison numbers; master.html has ~25 cards that are javascript:void(0) alert() popups of static text directly under a footer claiming "Every cell on this page links to a real endpoint. No mocks"; the MCP wrapper cited in FINAL_SUBMIT as compliance proof has a step() that would crash (unpacks a 4-tuple from a single object) and 3 of 6 tools call a method that does not exist; and the package client's step() sends a wrapped payload the server will 422. This is a strong engine wearing a partly cardboard costume.
